prompts: This is an instructional notebook. It is part of the Predictive Modeling Pipeline module of the Scikit-learn Associate Course. It introduces the core scikit-learn API by training a KNeighborsClassifier on a purely numerical version of the adult census dataset, making predictions, and evaluating generalization on a held-out test set. Key learning objectives are: (1) loading adult-census-numeric.csv, separating data (four numerical columns) from target using drop and column indexing; (2) understanding the three-method API: fit trains the model, predict generates predictions, and score computes accuracy; (3) recognizing that evaluating on training data is overly optimistic (~82%) compared to evaluating on a separate test set (~80%); (4) understanding why generalization to unseen data is the true measure of model quality. Expected outputs include: data with 39,073 samples and 4 features, target_predicted array, training accuracy of ~0.824, and test accuracy of ~0.804 using data_test and target_test from adult-census-numeric-test.csv. Students running this notebook must load adult-census-numeric.csv (not adult-census.csv): the full dataset contains categorical string columns that KNeighborsClassifier cannot process, causing a 'could not convert string to float' error or an 'Unknown label type' error. The n_neighbors value used here is the default (5); how to select this hyperparameter optimally is covered later in the hyperparameter tuning module. If the student asks a question that cannot be answered from this context alone, refer to https://inria.github.io/scikit-learn-mooc/python_scripts/02_numerical_pipeline_introduction.html. If asked about more information on the dataset, refer to https://inria.github.io/scikit-learn-mooc/python_scripts/datasets_adult_census.html
